Comparing numbers with known precision

Source: R/compare.R
sigfig-comparison.Rd

Comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) round both sides to their coarsest known precision, and give a logical vector. Values which display equally at the same precision are therefore always equal. Ordinary numbers are exact, so use the precision of the number they are compared with. Numbers are compared exactly when neither has known precision.

Details

Equality is not transitive when precision differs: 3.12 and 3.14 both equal 3.1, but not each other. So unique(), duplicated(), match(), sort(), order() and grouping instead use each element's own rounded value and its precision: 3.1 and 3.10 are distinct, with the coarser sorted first. All missing values are the same, regardless of their precision.

min(), max() and range() use the full value.

Examples

sigfig(3.14159, 2) == 3.14
#> [1] TRUE
sigfig(3.12, 2) == sigfig(3.1, 1)
#> [1] TRUE
unique(sigfig(c(3.1, 3.1, 3.12), c(1, 2, 1)))
#> <sigfig[2]>
#> [1]  3.1 3.10
